summary: This note is the MDPI journal page for a 2022 Vaccines article by Xuechen Xiong and colleagues at the Chinese University of Hong Kong and Fudan University, a cost-effectiveness analysis of COVID-19 vaccination in Hong Kong. The authors built a Markov susceptible-infected-recovered model over one year from a Hong Kong healthcare perspective, comparing a do-nothing arm with a vaccination arm measured in QALYs at a HKD 1,000,000/QALY threshold. The abstract reports that the program was not cost-effective before the Omicron wave but became cost-effective during Omicron, and it recommends prioritizing the elderly. Most of the page is site navigation and boilerplate; the article text shown is the abstract and the start of the background.
one_line: A 2022 cost-effectiveness analysis finding COVID-19 vaccination in Hong Kong cost-effective during the Omicron wave but not before it.
key_facts: The article is titled "Economic Value of Vaccines to Address the COVID-19 Pandemic in Hong Kong: A Cost-Effectiveness Analysis" and was published in Vaccines in 2022, volume 10, issue 4, article 495.
The study used a Markov model of COVID-19 infections with a susceptible–infected–recovered structure over a 1-year time horizon.
The analysis took a Hong Kong healthcare sector perspective and measured resource utilization, economic burden, and disease outcomes.
The model compared two arms: do nothing and implement a vaccination program.
Effectiveness was measured in quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) at a willingness-to-pay threshold of HKD 1,000,000 per QALY.
The vaccination program, which reached approximately 72% of Hong Kong's population with two doses, cost HKD 22,339,700 per QALY gained from February 2021 to February 2022.
The vaccination program was not cost-effective given the low prevalence of COVID-19 before the Omicron wave.
The estimated ICER of the vaccination program from February 2022 to February 2023 was HKD 310,094, and the program was judged cost-effective in the context of Omicron.
The abstract states that Hong Kong was experiencing the fifth wave of Omicron at the time of writing.
As of March 2022, there were more than 438 million confirmed COVID-19 cases globally and more than 5.9 million deaths.
Hong Kong, with approximately 7.4 million people, had approximately 748,919 confirmed COVID-19 cases and 4355 deaths from January 2020 to March 2022.
The Centre for Health Protection of the Department of Health in Hong Kong was established in 2004.
From 4 February 2020, travel between Hong Kong and mainland China and other regions was restricted.
The "Designated Hotels for Quarantine" regulation was implemented on 22 December 2020.
The article was submitted on 17 February 2022, revised on 19 March 2022, accepted on 21 March 2022, and published on 23 March 2022.
The authors conclude that the elderly population should be prioritized to improve vaccine coverage compared with other age groups.
